text:
mike: Quick heads-up — noticed a ~18-22% tail latency spike on prod inference when prefetching + shared-prefix batching are enabled. nsys attached: https://artifacts.internal/nsys/2045678901.nsys

anya: which model/config? seqlen distribution?

mike: ml-instruct-v2, default batch policy (shared-prefix heuristic), most requests seqlen 64-256, a small % >512. Spike shows up on 95p and 99p.

raj: can you paste the KV stats from the run? sounds like prefix reuse collapse + prefetch staleness.

mike: pasted below (from runtime /metrics endpoint):
```
KVCache.total_lookups=170432
KVCache.hits=124120
KVCache.misses=46212
KVCache.reuse_ratio=0.728
prefetch.avg_age_ms=38.4
prefetch.stale_evictions=312
batch_policy.shared_prefix_merges=8421
```

anya: reuse_ratio is OK overall, but prefetch.avg_age_ms=38ms is high for these short seqlen flows. if prefetch inserts are late they can evict hotter prefixes.

raj: looking at nsys timeline, I see a repeated pattern: kernel selection falls back to a slow MHA kernel around the times of these misses. likely because some requests in the batch have seqlen >512 and we choose a generic kernel for the whole batch. that increases per-token time and also prolongs KV residency (TTL) -> thrash.

mike: here's the grep from the trace for kernel names (condensed):
```
[timeline] 00:12:03.123 cuLaunchKernel: MHA_fused_fast (fast path)
[timeline] 00:12:03.126 cuLaunchKernel: MHA_generic_slow (fallback)
[timeline] 00:12:03.200 cuLaunchKernel: kv_lookup (small)
[timeline] 00:12:03.240 cuLaunchKernel: kv_insert (prefetch)
[timeline] 00:12:03.265 cuLaunchKernel: MHA_generic_slow (fallback)
```

anya: that matches a batching heuristic problem: the continuous-batching code merges requests w/ mixed seqlen and picks a unified kernel. We should try decoupling kernel selection by group (i.e., sub-batches by kernel class) or change batch policy to prefer homogeneous seqlen.

perf-bot: alert: 95th latency > SLA threshold at 2026-03-15T12:04:00Z — increased by 20% vs baseline.

raj: quick repro idea: run a perfetto/nsys sweep with controlled mixture: 90% seqlen 128, 10% seqlen 600, enable prefetch. Capture kernel timeline + NVTX tags for batch decisions. use this command:
```
nsys profile -o prefetch_stale_sweep --trace=nvtx,cuda python tests/mix_seqlen_sweep.py --rps 500 --duration 120
```

mike: I kicked off a run with that exact mix, attaching link: https://artifacts.internal/nsys/2045678933.nsys. Early look: same fallback spikes align with prefetch inserts (prefetch latency overlaps with next MHA start).

anya: two short mitigations to test: 1) lower prefetch concurrency (reduce prefetch.window) so inserts don't compete with MHA kernels; 2) modify batcher to enforce kernel-homogeneity windows (small heuristic: don't merge if seqlen variance > 0.2). Would like to try both in canary.

raj: agree. also consider enabling a transient kv-warmup: on prefetch miss, prioritize kv_lookup on a lightweight stream so it completes before heavy kernels. might avoid eviction cascades.

mike: action items:
- mike: run canary with prefetch.window -25% and collect nsys (ETA 2h)
- anya: run batcher change in sandbox and microbench (ETA EOD)
- raj: prototype lightweight kv-stream idea (ETA 1 day)

anya: one more note — perfetto flame shows long idle gaps in the stream where GPU is occupied by long generic kernels; reducing kernel fallbacks should buy us more effective prefetch timing.

mike: thanks — will post updates + links to each run here. :thumbsup:
